correctness.rationale: Eliminating a common root of x⁵+x+t and 5x⁴+1 gives t⁴=1 exactly in characteristic 23. For the Frobenius convention one can use the Čech classes y/x and y/x²: the coefficient in output row i, input column j is [x^(23j−i)](x⁵+x+t)^11. Independent expansion by occupied factor positions confirmed all four entries and det=2t⁴(t⁴+2). On t⁴=−2 the Frobenius matrix Mᵀ has image the first coordinate line and restricts there to the nonzero semilinear map z↦−5t z^23. Its stable rank is therefore exactly one, not an inference from one-step rank alone. With column vectors the two-step matrix is H H^(23); both orders of these two factors have the same image and nonzero eigenvalue 13 here. The zero and invertible matrices give stable ranks zero and two respectively. One-step ranks give the stated a-numbers, and a=2 is superspecial in dimension two. The determinant has order four at zero and all four other smooth roots are simple. Those roots lie in F529 by the multiplicative-order calculation and are not F23-rational since −2 is a nonsquare; the independent field replay confirmed all four. Under x=s²X, y=s⁵Y with s⁸=1 the parameter multiplies by s^(−2), acting transitively on the four roots; distinct p-rank separates their geometric curve from the center.
residual_risks: The nonordinary divisor is on the indicated smooth parameter line, not a statement about moduli multiplicities or singular fibers. The orbit conclusion is geometric, not a classification of twists over the field of definition.

evidence: Zhu's formula at these integers immediately gives determinant −90t⁸+27t⁴ and one-step ranks 0,1,2. Rank one of a one-step matrix by itself does not determine the stable Frobenius rank.

On the four nonzero zeros the specialized matrix preserves a line and acts invertibly there after Frobenius twisting. The scaling symmetry then gives a single geometric isomorphism class; the known central case does not imply that statement.

originality.rationale: Credit only the complete mixed geometric p-rank stratification of this characteristic-23 pencil and its nonzero exceptional isomorphism class. Zhu's coefficient formula covers the determinant and one-step ranks by substitution, and the central superspecial curve is classical. Neither the generic-ordinarity theorem nor the sources on the central curve supply the exceptional stable Frobenius rank and the full pencil-orbit classification. No matching characteristic-23 statement was identified in the bounded primary and catalogue comparisons.
residual_risks: Other historical curve tables or a different presentation of the rank-one orbit could overlap. The access limitation and catalogue nonreturn are not evidence of priority.

value.rationale: For the standard sparse hyperelliptic pencil, understanding where ordinary fibers degenerate and distinguishing stable ranks there is a natural classification problem, not just a coefficient evaluation. An independent smaller-odd-prime screen supports the relevance of 23: at 3, 11, 17 and 19 the center is ordinary; at 5 and 7 the determinant vanishes identically; at 13 it is a nonzero multiple of t⁴, giving no second nonordinary parameter. At 23 a superspecial center coexists with both an ordinary generic fiber and a separate rank-one exceptional class. The four-to-one relation between nonzero parameter presentations and the single geometric class and the divisor multiplicities are useful exact data about that transition.
residual_risks: The lower-prime screen motivates this exact regime; it is not a claimed classification of all smaller-prime fibers or of all characteristics. The result does not classify all genus-two curves over F23 or F529.
